title: Closures and Captured Variables
learning_outcomes: Explain the role of closures and captured variables in a Ruby program and name the key rule involved.
Apply closures and captured variables in a small example and predict its result before running it.
Identify one boundary or failure case related to closure behavior across method calls and verify the intended behavior.

content.intro: Learn Closures and Captured Variables through a visual model, a minimal Ruby example, and a practical check.
content.why_it_matters: Understanding closures and captured variables helps you write code that is easier to explain, test, and maintain. It also helps separate Ruby language guarantees from runtime assumptions, dependency behavior, and application-specific rules.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Closures and Captured Variables helps you reason about capturing surrounding variables. In Ruby, prefer a small example whose inputs and expected result are easy to explain. This lesson connects the syllabus topic to practical code and highlights where assumptions or edge cases matter.

content_blocks.title: How to think about it
content_blocks.text: Begin by identifying the key rule: Capturing surrounding variables. Then connect it to Persistent local state. The remaining syllabus points—Closure behavior across method calls—are useful checks before applying this in a larger project.

content_blocks.title: Example: Closures and Captured Variables
content_blocks.code:
def counter
  count = 0
  -> { count += 1 }
end
c = counter
puts c.call
puts c.call

content_blocks.title: Guided example
content_blocks.text: Run the example as written, compare it with the expected result, and explain why each line supports closures and captured variables. Next change one input or condition and predict the result before running it.

content_blocks.title: Try it yourself
content_blocks.text: Create a second example for closures and captured variables using a different input. Add one edge case from the syllabus list (Closure behavior across method calls), state the expected behavior, and write a small test or manual check that would catch a regression.

content_blocks.title: Recap
content_blocks.text: You should now be able to explain closures and captured variables, identify its place in blocks, procs, lambdas, and closures, run a focused example, and verify an important boundary. Revisit the linked exercise if this is a core topic; advanced runtime or framework examples remain draft until reviewed in a suitable environment.
